title: Sunny and the Baby Echidna | Bedtime Story
description: When Sunny the little quokka discovers a tiny baby echidna who has rolled into a ball because the world looks so big, she sits nearby and talks softly until the night feels safe. A tender bedtime story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories, perfect for little ones who need reassurance at bedtime.
narration:
The last birds had finished their evening songs, and the bush was settling into a soft, purple quiet. Sunny the little quokka was taking her slow, sleepy walk along the edge of the old fallen log when she noticed something she had never seen before.

There, right beside the log, was a tiny spiky ball. Just about as big as Sunny's paw. It was a puggle — a baby echidna — who had crept out from under the log for the very first time. And when everything looked so big and the shadows grew so long, the little puggle had done what baby echidnas do. She had tucked her nose down, curled her legs in tight, and rolled into a perfect, spiky little ball.

Sunny stopped. She didn't move any closer. She knew it was important to be very, very gentle.

She sat down quietly, a little way off, and she began to talk in her softest voice.

"The night is kind," Sunny said. "The dark isn't scary. It's just the bush pulling a big blanket over everything so everyone can rest."

She paused and listened to the quiet.

"The stars are coming out now. They're very small and very gentle, just like you."

For a long moment, nothing moved. Then, slowly — ever so slowly — the spiky ball began to uncurl. A tiny black nose appeared. Two small dark eyes blinked at the night. The puggle sniffed the air, smelling the eucalyptus and the cool earth, and seemed to understand that the night was exactly as kind as Sunny had said.

Then, with the most careful little shuffle, the puggle tucked herself back safely under the log to sleep.

Sunny smiled the softest smile and curled up right there beside the log, and let the quiet night hold them both.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little puggle. Goodnight, little one.
